candidate_sources.docs/host-api.md: createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled. Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

checkpoints: During one editing burst, multiple edits reset the 120 ms timer and only the latest text is written after 120 ms of quiet.
After one burst is consumed, a later edit starts a new burst and is saved normally.
An empty-string edit is retained and saved, rather than being confused with absence of pending work.
Editing with no current Badge remains a no-op.
Pending text remains associated with the document that was current when Edit accepted it, including across open, close, and dispose transitions.
Opening or closing with pending text preserves persistence and synchronous navigation behavior: stale outer Open work must not overwrite a navigation initiated by the save callback.
The departing Badge subscription is stopped, and status output remains filtered to events for that Badge's document.
Preview still uses its 40 ms trailing task, and Hide still cancels its pending preview.
After an Action, run the public Go syntax/build check with generated binaries and caches outside /workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not write each accepted editor edit directly to the store.
Do not redirect pending text to whichever document happens to be current when the timer fires.
Do not cancel or discard an accepted document edit merely because its Badge is detached or the workspace navigates, closes, or disposes.
Do not allow a superseded outer Open to install or render its requested document after a save callback synchronously navigates.
Do not duplicate a pending write during reentrant flushing, or erase a new burst accepted during the prior burst's consumer callback.
Do not change Store event identity, text, revision, listener ordering, or current-document status filtering.
Do not change search-preview timing or cancellation behavior.
Do not edit tests or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: Each document ID owns one reusable Trailing buffer in the workspace coordinator dictionary.
A Badge represents only the current view and owns its document-specific live Store subscription; retiring the Badge must not destroy the document buffer.
An edit is bound at acceptance time to the current Badge's document buffer.
Workspace generation identifies the currently authoritative navigation request; a save-triggered nested navigation supersedes the outer request.
Pending state represents the latest text of one burst and is cleared before its save callback runs, allowing a subsequent burst to be established independently.

obligations.text: Change Workspace.Edit so that, when a current Badge exists, it pushes the supplied text into that Badge's document buffer instead of writing immediately; with no current Badge it remains a no-op.
Use the existing Trailing utility with a 120 ms delay for editor buffers, resetting the timer on each edit and writing only the latest text after the quiet interval.
Reuse one editor buffer per document ID from the workspace coordinator dictionary so pending work keeps its original document association across view changes.

Ensure consuming a burst retires its pending value and timer handle before invoking the write callback, preserving empty strings, preventing duplicate reentrant consumption, and allowing later bursts to save.

When retiring a current Badge, revoke current ownership, detach its captured subscription, preserve the existing document-clearing effect, and flush its accepted pending buffer so navigation, close, and dispose do not weaken the prior synchronous persistence behavior.
Because flushing may synchronously invoke navigation through Store listeners, Open must revalidate its captured generation after retirement before installing or rendering the requested destination.
Preserve Store read/write/event semantics, document and status output payloads, subscription cleanup, and all existing public Workspace methods.
Leave Preview behavior unchanged, including its separate 40 ms quiet interval and Hide cancellation.

ordering_barriers: Workspace.Edit must capture the current Badge and push into that Badge's buffer; document selection must not be deferred until timer consumption.
Trailing.Flush must snapshot the pending text and clear both handle and pending state before calling its work function.
Workspace retirement must capture the departing Badge and set current to nil before any pending save can invoke synchronous navigation.

The departing subscription and document-clearing presentation must be completed before flushing the departing buffer, so nested navigation can establish the successor without later stale retirement effects.

Workspace.Open must increment and capture generation before retirement, then compare that request with the current generation after retirement returns and before creating a Badge, reading the destination, or emitting destination document output.
A destination Store read must occur only after departure flushing, so it observes any pending save, including a same-document reopen.
preservation: Preserve createWorkspace behavior and the Open, Edit, Close, and Dispose public surface represented by the existing Workspace methods.
Preserve document output with the requested ID and the Store's current text, plus document clearing on retirement.
Preserve synchronous Store writes and notifications, monotonically increasing revision values, sorted listener notification order, and event fields id, text, and revision.
Preserve status publication only when an event ID matches the live Badge's document ID.
Preserve subscription removal when a Badge retires.
Preserve independent buffers for different document IDs and reuse of a document's buffer across visits.
Preserve accepted string text exactly, including empty strings.
Preserve Preview.Query trailing publication at 40 ms and Preview.Hide cancellation.
scope: Business behavior in /workspace/src/workflow.go for workspace editor buffering, Badge retirement, and navigation authority.
The existing Trailing utility is the required scheduling mechanism where appropriate.
Public documentation and source supplied in TASK, README.md, docs/host-api.md, and src/workflow.go are normative.
Search preview is explicitly outside the maintenance change except that its existing behavior must be preserved.

Harbor logistics — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: coordinator dictionary

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.

Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

triggers: Workspace.Edit(text) while a Badge is current.
Expiration of the editor buffer's 120 ms timer after no newer edit.
Workspace.Open(id), Workspace.Close(), or Workspace.Dispose() while a document buffer has pending text.
A synchronous Store listener invoking navigation during a buffered save.
Preview.Query(text) and Preview.Hide(), solely as unchanged behavior boundaries.
unknowns: TASK does not explicitly state a departure-flush deadline; flushing before retirement returns is derived from preserving the original immediate-write persistence behavior and ensuring destination reads are fresh.
Public sources establish synchronous navigation from Store listeners, but do not specify exception handling for timer, write, subscription, or output callbacks.

The Environment.Write implementation is not supplied; the contract preserves its existing use as the editor buffer consumer without assuming behavior beyond the documented synchronous Store/listener boundary.
No public behavioral tests are supplied; VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states that public checks validate syntax/build rather than business behavior.
Whether Environment.Output callbacks can navigate is not specified, so no additional output-callback reentrancy requirement is inferred.
BufferBank is defined but Workspace currently maintains its own coordinator dictionary; the normative ownership requirement is dictionary reuse, not mandatory use of the BufferBank type.
